observationsNotFindings: This is the first coexistence case in the sweep and it is handled well enough to be worth naming as a pattern. Two leftover-joins now cover G18: this one on the gate row DR-G18 with token OPEN, and lifecycle-leftover-join.v2 on the register row DR-107 with token PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW. They share four obligation ids and agree on every one. Each names the other and states which row it serves. The hazard in this shape is silent divergence - two artifacts asserting different dispositions for the same obligation id - and a coordinator recording either one should re-check that agreement rather than assume it, because nothing structural prevents a future version of one from drifting.

The token risk here is the most acute in the sweep. Elsewhere the wrong token would have been a neighbouring row's; here the two rows cover the same lifecycle subject matter, and DR-107 is further along at PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW than DR-G18 at OPEN. Importing it would have made the gate look closer to closure than it is. The artifact refuses it in four places including a dedicated doesNot entry.

OBL-ENCODING-NOT-STOLEN is the counterpart move to OBL-ENCODING-RESERVED and it is the right one. Rather than restating the reserved-mechanism obligation on the gate row, this join carries a non-acquisition obligation that points at DR-107 and confirms the standing is still true there. That keeps one obligation with one owner while making the boundary visible from both sides.

OBL-G18-FX-AUTHORING is the single open obligation and it is the same obligation the DR-107 join also carries open. The remaining fixture work for the three corpus classes is therefore counted on both rows, which is accurate but means a reader tallying open leftovers across rows should not double-count it.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. The land test passes and is the most acute instance of it in the sweep: DR-G18's live status cell reads OPEN while DR-107's reads PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, the two rows cover the same lifecycle subject matter, and importing DR-107's token would have made the gate look closer to closure than it is. The subject carries OPEN and refuses the import in four places including a dedicated doesNot entry. The structural question this artifact raises is coexistence: it is the gate-row leftover-join for G18 while lifecycle-leftover-join.v2 is the register-row leftover-join for DR-107, and they share four obligation ids. I compared all four on both leftoverDesign and rideStanding and found zero disagreements, and each artifact names the other and states which row it serves. That hazard is silent divergence rather than duplication, so a coordinator recording either should re-check the agreement rather than assume it - nothing structural prevents a future version of one from drifting. OBL-ENCODING-RESERVED is not restated here; instead OBL-ENCODING-NOT-STOLEN points at DR-107 and confirms the standing is still true there, which I verified. The three-member corpus list equals both live G18 v2 and the catalog under ==, and probing for concrete journal or lock encodings returns nothing. Disclosure: two of the three review pins are mine, including the lifecycle join this artifact must be checked against, so I made that comparison between the two artifacts' obligation objects rather than between verdicts. 18 attacks run, 18 refuted.
